publication.heroTitle: A clearer world in three cards
publication.heroDescription: Essential science and technology news, simplified.

sections.title: People & Politics
sections.description: Important developments in governments, societies and the people shaping the world.

cards.title: Mysterious groups spend millions targeting Republicans in 2026 midterms
cards.content: A mysterious network of political organizations, including Our Heritage Matters, American Forge Coalition, and Patriotic Duty Initiative, spent millions of dollars targeting Republican candidates in the 2026 midterm elections. These groups, which emerged suddenly and disappeared just as quickly, used robocalls, text messages, and political mailers to accuse Republican candidates of being insufficiently conservative and promote little-known Libertarian or third-party candidates as the true conservative alternatives. While the organizations claimed to be concerned with issues like gun rights, immigration, and national security, their messaging was often misleading or false. The groups' tactics are part of a broader trend of opaque and often misleading political spending, which has grown in scale and influence since the Supreme Court's 2010 Citizens United decision.

cards.title: US Air Force Responds to Suspected Drone Activity Over RAF Lakenheath
cards.content: US Air Force responded to suspected unauthorized drone activity over RAF Lakenheath in Suffolk on Friday evening. No personnel, aircraft, or infrastructure were affected, according to a spokesperson. The incident comes after unconfirmed reports of sirens sounding at the base, which residents reported hearing from a nearby village. Authorities have resolved the situation, and no threat to the public was reported. This incident follows heightened security activity at US bases in the UK after an incident at RAF Fairford in September, which Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Iran was involved in. The US removed its bombers from the base in October, and the British government has insisted that airbases are safe and their security is a top priority.

cards.title: Trump Meets Xi and Putin on Nuclear Non-Proliferation at APEC Summit
cards.content: US President Donald Trump will hold a historic meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin next week, focusing on nuclear non-proliferation. The meeting, set to take place at the APEC summit in China, aims to discuss reducing nuclear weapons globally, a topic Trump believes is dangerous. Although officials downplay the possibility of a new agreement, the meeting is seen as a starting point for future talks. The leaders will also discuss Iran. Elon Musk is expected to accompany Trump, but will not attend the trilateral meeting. This marks the first-ever joint meeting between the leaders of the three countries.

sections.title: Science and technology
sections.description: Discover breakthroughs in science, space, computing and emerging technology.

cards.title: Venice's historic buildings face preservation challenge due to floods
cards.content: Venice's architectural legacy faces a growing preservation challenge due to floods and environmental factors. Innovative technologies, such as drone photography, terrestrial laser scanning, and photogrammetry, are being used to create digital models of historic buildings, like the Church of San Francesco della Vigna, to detect signs of damage and aging earlier. The digital mapping helps identify areas where stonework has deteriorated, and the models provide further information about cracks and areas where structural stresses could be concentrated. The project's goal is to create a detailed digital record, which can be used to support future conservation work and long-term monitoring of the building's condition.

cards.title: Prehistoric Whale Had Extreme Facial Asymmetry, Scientists Find
cards.content: Scientists have discovered a prehistoric whale, Scaphokogia huachafo, that lived around 6.3 to 5.6 million years ago. The whale's skull had the most extreme facial asymmetry ever documented in a mammal, with its bony nostrils displaced entirely to the left and its snout curved sharply downward. Researchers believe the whale's unusual anatomy suggests it had a feeding strategy that differed from modern sperm whales, which hunt deep ocean waters. Instead, Scaphokogia huachafo appears to have been adapted for searching for food along the bottom of shallow coastal seas. Its unique snout and neck allowed it to move directly above the seabed and feed close to the sediment.

cards.title: Nvidia's Crisis Creates Shift in AI Chip Industry, Stocks Surge for Rivals
cards.content: The news article reports on the ongoing crisis at Nvidia, which has led to a leadership void and a potential shift in the company's grip on the AI chip industry. As investors bet on Nvidia's competitors, including AMD, Broadcom, and TSMC, to close the technological gap, these companies' stocks are gaining momentum. TSMC, which manufactures Nvidia's most advanced processors, has rallied 11% over the past week. Meanwhile, other semiconductor stocks, such as Texas Instruments, Analog Devices, and Infineon, have also seen significant gains. Experts believe that Huang's departure could fundamentally reshape competition across the AI supply chain, giving companies like Google and Amazon an opportunity to expand their AI chip production. The ongoing investigations and management uncertainty at Nvidia may continue to impact the company's stock, but experts suggest that the broader AI investment cycle remains intact, with major technology companies projecting higher AI spending in 2027. The article highlights the potential reshuffling of winners within the semiconductor industry, as investors rotate and diversify their portfolios.

sections.title: Health & wellness
sections.description: Medical research, public health and discoveries that affect everyday wellbeing.

cards.title: US Reports 10 Measles Deaths in Worst Year Since 1991
cards.content: The United States is experiencing its worst measles year since 1991, with 10 deaths reported so far, and has lost its official measles elimination status. The country had achieved measles elimination in 2000, but falling vaccination rates and denial of the vaccine's safety have led to a resurgence of the disease. Public health experts are warning that regaining elimination status will be harder this time due to lack of trust in the public health system and science, as well as changes in the epidemiology of measles. They stress that the solution lies in strong leadership and a renewed focus on vaccination, citing the power of vaccination in controlling the disease.

cards.title: ER Doctor Fails to Recognize Rare Condition, Baby Dies
cards.content: Stephanie and Eric Biesenbach took their 11-day-old daughter Gwen to the emergency room when she started bleeding from her belly button. Despite the ER doctor, Nicole Malouf, trying various methods to stop the bleeding, Gwen's condition continued to deteriorate. Malouf failed to recognize the signs of vitamin K deficiency bleeding, a rare but potentially life-threatening condition, and did not give Gwen the vitamin K shot. Gwen's bleeding worsened, and she eventually died. An investigation by the Texas Medical Board found that Malouf had failed to meet the standard of care in her treatment of Gwen and that her lack of timely care ultimately resulted in Gwen's death. Malouf was required to take 24 hours of continuing medical education and inform her employers of the disciplinary action taken against her.

sections.title: Environment
sections.description: Climate, oceans, ecosystems and the changing planet around us.

cards.title: CO2 Emissions Reach 40 Billion Tonnes, Threatening 1.5°C Threshold
cards.content: The world's CO2 emissions have increased to nearly 40 billion tonnes per year due to fossil-fuel-driven industrialisation, causing the planet to warm by about 1.3-1.4°C above pre-industrial levels. If everyone lived like the average American, the warming would be around 3.7°C, while living like the average Qatari would push warming to over 5°C. On the other hand, if everyone lived like the average Indian, the warming would be lower, at around 0.8°C. Historically, the Chinese lifestyle has had a much lower impact, with warming of only 1.2°C. The United Nations Environment Programme warns that overshooting the 1.5°C threshold is likely within the next three to four years.

cards.title: Human metabolism's carbon dioxide emissions rise 74% in 30 years
cards.content: A new study by the University of Bath has found that the amount of carbon dioxide produced by human metabolism has increased by 74% over the past three decades, with the global total reaching an estimated 2.05 billion metric tons annually by 2015. The study, published in The Lancet Planetary Health, analyzed thousands of real-world measurements of CO2 production in people of all ages and found that the increase is mainly due to population growth, with more than 60% of the rise attributed to an increase in the number of people rather than a significant change in the amount produced by each individual. The researchers suggest that accounting for this activity could help scientists more accurately predict how effective carbon reduction strategies may be.

cards.title: Srinagar's Water Crisis Worsens due to Climate Change
cards.content: In Srinagar, a water crisis has been ongoing for years, causing daily struggles for residents like Mehak and Zamrood. The absence of a regular water supply has led to the installation of tanks and a hand pump at their homes. Climate change is affecting Doodh Ganga, a vital source of drinking water, causing erratic water supply, low flow, and dry taps. The river's water availability is decreasing due to rising temperatures, changing rainfall patterns, and declining snowmelt. The Kashmir Valley's 24 watersheds, including Doodh Ganga, are experiencing similar impacts.

sections.title: Entertainment
sections.description: Stories from film, music, sports, culture and the world of entertainment.

cards.title: Cornwall Festivals Get Approval to Host Thousands More
cards.content: Two music festivals in Cornwall, The Great Estate and Live at Scorrier House, have received permission to increase their attendance by thousands. The festivals, held within the grounds of Scorrier House, will now be allowed to accommodate 14,999 people each, up from 12,000 and 9,999 respectively. The increased capacity was approved by a Cornwall Council licensing committee, which heard that the events would bring in millions to the local economy and support Cornish jobs and businesses. The committee added conditions to the increased capacity, including security measures to prevent festivalgoers from trespassing on neighboring properties.

cards.title: Eurovision introduces Asia edition, featuring 11 countries in Bangkok
cards.content: The European Broadcasting Union is introducing Eurovision Asia, the first-ever Asian edition of the 70-year-old song contest, to celebrate its 70th anniversary. The contest, held in Bangkok, will feature 11 countries from the region, including Thailand, Malaysia, and the Philippines. Unlike European versions, the Asian edition will not focus on singer popularity, but on the song itself. However, the organization has faced issues, including a sudden budget cut, staff resignations, and concerns about the voting system, which will combine public and jury votes. Eurovision Asia is an experiment to bring the popular contest to a new region, but it remains to be seen how audiences will adjust to this new format.

cards.title: Rosalía wins best album award three times at Latin Grammys
cards.content: Rosalía made history at the Latin Grammys, becoming the first woman to win the best album award three times. She won five awards, including two for her song La Perla, which was also nominated for record of the year. Rosalía expressed gratitude to those who doubted her, saying she didn't listen to their negative opinions. Additionally, Daddy Yankee won the person of the year award, and Punjabi singer Diljit Dosanjh made his debut at the Latin Grammys, performing alongside Daddy Yankee. The event also saw Milo J win record of the year, and ARIA VEGA and Sara Schell win best new artist and songwriter of the year, respectively.

sections.title: economy
sections.description: Markets, businesses, trade and economic changes shaping the global economy.

cards.title: Microsoft Outage Hits Millions, Affects Schools, Healthcare, and Governments
cards.content: A global Microsoft outage, which started Thursday, has been affecting schools, healthcare systems, businesses, courts, and governments worldwide, impacting millions of users. The outage, caused by a technical issue, has led to connectivity problems, with users unable to send or receive emails, access certain files, or view their calendar apps. Microsoft has apologized for the disruption and is working to restore services, but warns that some users may still experience intermittent issues. The outage has had a significant impact, with many organizations and institutions affected, including OpenAI and Anthropic, and has caused disruptions to services like email and online meetings.

cards.title: AI-Enhanced Images Raise Concerns of Misleading Homebuyers
cards.content: Estate agents are increasingly using AI to enhance property images, making homes seem more appealing. However, this practice, dubbed 'housefishing', has raised concerns among experts and homebuyers that it can mislead and waste time. Olivia Nicole, 29, was shocked to find that a five-bedroom property she viewed had been significantly altered from its online listing, with smaller rooms, different decor, and structural features changed. The AI-enhanced images, used on Rightmove, Zoopla, and Winkworth, were not clearly labeled as such, leading Olivia to feel her time was wasted. Experts warn that estate agents must use AI responsibly, labeling enhanced images and avoiding structural changes that can mislead consumers. As the trend continues to grow, concerns are rising that AI-enhanced images may become more widespread, potentially leading to more instances of 'housefishing'.

cards.title: Nscale to Build UK's Largest AI Data Centre in Loughton, Despite Microsoft Pullout
cards.content: Nscale, a tech company, has reaffirmed its plans to build the UK's largest AI data centre in Loughton, Essex, despite Microsoft's decision to pull out of the project. Microsoft had agreed to fund a supercomputer at the site, but its involvement has been terminated. Nscale is exploring alternative power sources and maintaining a strong relationship with Microsoft for other projects globally. The data centre was expected to receive its power supply by the end of this year, but this has been delayed until the 2030s due to a London-wide grid issue. The project is expected to create 250 permanent jobs when it opens.
